A classification system can be inserted for closed-circuit operation, or the product can be discharged directly in open circuit. Both modes are easy to operate and convenient to manage, enabling continuous, stable industrial production. During comminution the tower mill can also carry out physical adsorption and chemical reactions of the product at the same time. Low noise, low vibration and low heat generation. The grinding media in the tower mill move in an orderly manner, reducing ineffective collisions and unproductive power consumption and thus reducing noise, vibration and heat generation; no cooling device is required. The tower mill occupies little space and has no external rotating parts. Its internal forces are fully balanced on a macroscopic scale, so its foundation bears only the net weight. Foundation work is therefore simple, installation time is short, the equipment is safe and it can be installed outdoors.
177: The tower mill operates as follows: as the stirring screw rotates slowly, centrifugal force, gravity and friction cause the grinding media and the material to circulate in an orderly manner, with forces approximately balanced on a macroscopic scale. Within the stirring screw they rise helically at less than the lifting speed; between the lining and the outer edge of the screw they descend helically. On a microscopic scale, however, uneven forces produce dynamic differences in velocity and changes in force. These subject the material to strong compression and grinding, combined with breakage under forces between particles, microshearing and splitting. Material of the required fineness rises with the conveying medium, undergoes internal classification and flows freely out of the upper part of the tower mill body.
178: The tower mill’s operating principle is also reflected in the high degree of packing between the grinding media and the material. There are few collisions between balls or between the balls and the tower mill lining or stirring screw. The macroscopic balancing of forces throughout the rotating assembly imposes very small loads on the support system, and energy consumption in the bearings is also very low. Fine material always reaches the vicinity of the discharge outlet more readily than coarse material, making internal classification during comminution easier and greatly reducing overgrinding. In addition, the tower mill’s internal classification is relatively easy to match to an external classification system, allowing production of powders with a very narrow particle size distribution.
179: The tower mill operates on the principle of a stirred mill, but its rotational speed is lower than that of other stirred mills. In addition, the agitated media roll in an orderly manner, so the tower mill is also suitable for manufacture in larger sizes to meet the needs of large-scale production.

190: Because high-pressure grinding rolls look much like a conventional double-roll crusher, many people mistakenly believe they share its drawbacks. In fact, high-pressure roll grinding differs fundamentally from conventional comminution in two ways. First, it uses quasi-static compression, which saves about 30% of the energy used in impact crushing [2]. Second, it crushes a bed of material: the particles crush one another. Compared with conventional crushing and ball milling, this principle markedly improves comminution efficiency and markedly reduces wear. The compressive stress between particles can be adjusted via the roll pressure. Two counter-rotating rolls perform the entire grinding process; one roll is fixed and the other can move.
191: It can replace a power-intensive, inefficient ball-mill pregrinding system and reduce steel consumption and noise. Suitable for new plants as well as technical upgrades to existing plants, it increases ball-mill system output by 30–50%. In the pressed cake, 0.08 mm fines account for 20–35% and particles smaller than 2 mm account for 65–85%. Compression fills the internal structure of small particles with many tiny cracks, greatly improving grindability. The rolls are surfaced by hot weld overlay, making the wear-resistant layer easier to repair.
192: Based on actual results obtained with roller presses in the cement industry, the following main characteristics have been identified:
193: (1) Increased output: When a roller press is installed in the grinding system, its high-pressure load is transmitted through the diameters of the two rolls to the bed of material being ground. Most energy goes into compressing particles against one another. Sound and heat energy generated by friction between particles is converted into deformation energy, deforming, tearing and crushing them. This makes full use of the grinding equipment’s potential, increasing output by 50–100% and potentially reducing total energy consumption by 20%–30%, improving the productivity of the entire system.
194: (2) Reduced electricity consumption: Grind the material with a roller press. After pressing, not only is the particle size greatly reduced, but the Bond work index also falls markedly. This greatly improves grinding conditions in the downstream mill and markedly reduces the specific electricity consumption of the entire grinding system. It can significantly reduce the grinding system’s total electricity consumption. Energy savings are 25–50% compared with conventional grinding, with considerable annual benefits from electricity savings.
195: (3) Investment savings: Compared with a tube mill of the same required capacity, the roller press is simpler, smaller and lighter and takes up less plant space, saving on civil works and also facilitating retrofits to existing grinding systems. In addition, the roller press is very simple to operate and maintain.
196: (4) Good working environment: Material is continuously and steadily crushed by compression inside the roll enclosure, so harmful dust does not readily disperse. Furthermore, because there is practically no impact, the roller press is much quieter than a tube mill.
197: (5) Easy to scale up: Conventional tube mills are subject to machining, transport, heat-treatment and other constraints that severely limit increases in size. Grinding systems equipped with roller presses effectively solve such problems. Scaling up grinding systems has thus become a reality.
198: The roller press is designed on the principle of material-bed grinding. Its main features are high pressure, full speed, full feed and material-bed crushing. It consists of two compression rolls rotating synchronously in opposite directions, one fixed and one movable.
199: Material is fed from above the two rolls and continuously drawn between them. Under a high pressure of 100–150 MPa, it becomes a dense cake discharged from the bottom of the machine. The discharged cake contains a certain proportion of finished fine particles. Numerous cracks form inside the particles not yet at finished size, improving grindability and substantially reducing grinding energy consumption during further comminution.
200: Passage of the material through the grinding rolls has three main stages: full-feed densification, interparticle compression crushing and discharge in agglomerates.
201: A conventional roller press consists of a frame, two roll assemblies, a drive, a torque support, a roll enclosure, a feed device, a hydraulic (pressurizing) system, a main-bearing lubrication system, a grease lubrication system, an electrical system, a roll-removal device and other parts. In addition to the main parts and devices of a conventional press, a precision roller press has a device to ensure calendering accuracy.
